newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire stands firm against latest U.N. force plan.
newsitem.headline: Zaire stands firm against latest U.N. force plan.

text.p: Zaire's interior minister met the Canadian commander of a planned multinational force for Zaire on Saturday and later rejected Canada's proposal for airdropping supplies for war refugees in eastern Zaire.

"We do not understand how the multinational force could operate in Zaire without taking into account...the fact that we are at war with the regular armies of Rwanda and Burundi, supported by Uganda," Interior Minister Kamanda Wa Kamanda said.
"We remain formally against the airdropping of supplies," said Kamanda, speaking after meeting Canadian General Maurice Baril who was on a one-day visit to Kinshasa.
Zaire was also against the setting up of the U.N. military headquarters in Entebbe, Uganda, Kamanda told reporters.

Ambassadors from 14 countries meeting in Ottawa on Friday gave the green light for deployment of a multinational force commanded by Baril to bring aid to hundreds of thousands of Rwandan Hutu refugees and Zaireans displaced by recent fighting between the Zairean army and Rwanda-backed rebels.

More than 20 countries including the United States, France, Britain, Belgium, Senegal and South Africa, will contribute to the U.N. mission, more likely to comprise 1,000 or 2,000 troops instead of the 10,000 originally planned.

Baril recommended earlier this week that supplies be airdropped to the refugees but the Zairean government as well as relief agencies have poured scorn on the U.S.-backed prpoposal, saying it is dangerous and unworkable on the ground.
Baril said he was travelling on to Uganda later on Saturday. From there he would let his superiors know the position of the Zairean government and try to incorporate it into plans.

"Our mission is strictly humanitarian and has absolutely no political or military angles. We will not involve ourselves in disputes on the ground and will not coordinate with whoever controls the territory," he said.
Ever since proposals for an international military intervention in Zaire were first mooted early in November, Zaire has insisted the operation be led from bases on its territory.
But Baril proposes setting up his military headquarters in Entebbe, Uganda, where he is already based.
On Thursday the Canadian General met rebel leader Laurent Kabila, in the Zairean town of Goma on the Rwandan border.
Rwandan-backed rebels seized a swathe of territory in Eastern Zaire including Goma, having routed the poorly-equipped Zairean troops there in late October and early November.

Baril's visit to Goma has infuriated the Zairean government. On Friday, governement spokesman Boguo Makeli accused the Canandian general of violating Zaire's territorial integrity and recognising the legitimacy of rebel authorities.
With over half a million of the estimated 1.2 million Hutu refugees already back home in Rwanda, the government in Kigali maintains that the international force in Zaire is no longer necessary.
